correctness.rationale: For every spin j, the SO(3) central Peter–Weyl kernel contribution is (2j+1)χ_j with χ_j(θ)=sin((2j+1)θ)/sinθ; Weyl integration with 2sin²θ/π converts its convolution L1 and L∞ norm to the L1 weighted trigonometric kernel, with no restriction of input functions to classes. Differentiating the elementary odd-cosine Dirichlet sum gives exact B_L=−(L+1)cos(2(L+1)θ)+0.5 cotθ sin(2(L+1)θ). Removing spin L−1 and using product-to-sum identities yields leading −(L+1)(2cos2θ−1)cos(2Lθ), with a cot remainder of L1 O(log(L+2)) and a uniformly bounded sin remainder. Periodic |cos| mean 2/π and bounded variation of |2cos2θ−1| show an O(1/L) averaging error; the exact angular integral π/3+2sqrt(3) gives leading coefficients 4/π and 4/(3π)+8sqrt(3)/π². Their ratio 1/3+2sqrt(3)/π>1, yielding strict asymptotic inflation; no claim of finite-L monotonicity. Independent direct character-sum identities and quadrature at L=30,100 corroborate but do not establish the asymptotics.

value.rationale: Deleting one large representation sector from an orthogonal projector can unexpectedly increase its endpoint norm by a positive linear fraction of cutoff size. The exact SO(3) coefficient and ratio identify a natural sharp failure of monotonicity for Fourier spectral masks; the cancellation geometry is intrinsic to the group and representation index, and this phenomenon is not captured by generic norm-growth estimates.

limitations: Only large-integer-L asymptotics of contiguous SO3 cutoff minus L−1 spin; finite-L increase and other holes unproved.
